metadata.description: Lyngon devkit: the Claude Code plugin marketplace of the shared foundation for Lyngon software development. Plugins by concern, holding in-house and vetted vendored skills, plus pinned third-party plugins.

plugins.name: all
plugins.description: Every plugin a Lyngon repository uses, installed with one command. A bundle: it has no skills of its own.

plugins.name: repo
plugins.description: Set up or adopt a repository to Lyngon conventions (interview, INTENT.md, the agent file, README, CONCEPTS.md, decision records, devenv, git hooks) and create packages in the kind-first layout.

plugins.name: discover
plugins.description: Discovery before building: toss ideas around without writing anything, sharpen a design with a relentless interview that writes CONCEPTS.md terms and decision records as they crystallise and gates implementation on approval, or find out why code is the way it is from the decision records, git, pull requests and issues.

plugins.name: build
plugins.description: From an approved design to an open pull request: a plan of test-first tasks, executed inline or with a fresh subagent per task, a ledger that survives compaction, a review after every task and a whole-branch review at the end.

plugins.name: practice
plugins.description: Engineering discipline while changing code: test-driven development, systematic debugging and verification before any claim of done. Invoked by the agent on its own.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Code review both ways: dispatch a reviewer subagent with a crafted brief and a commit range, and receive review feedback with technical rigour instead of performative agreement.

plugins.name: devkit
plugins.description: Maintain the Lyngon devkit itself: add third-party or new skills to the marketplace with vetting, provenance and placement by concern.

plugins.name: writing
plugins.description: Prose quality: edit documentation, READMEs, posts and other non-code text so it reads as written by a person.

plugins.name: conventions
plugins.description: Organization-wide conventions, invoked by the agent before it works: engineering rules for every change, one skill per language, and the rules for Markdown, decision records and the steering documents.

plugins.name: principles
plugins.description: The principles Lyngon agents apply with judgment: an index the agent reads before work that takes judgment, and one file per principle, vendored from pstack or written by Lyngon.

plugins.name: skill-creator
plugins.description: Anthropic's skill authoring plugin: create, evaluate, improve and benchmark skills. Pinned; used by /devkit:add-skill to draft new in-house skills.
